    A[i, j]: inout num_t = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Temporaries used only during initialization (can share storage with A
    # in an implementation that pipelines stages):
    A0[i, j]: temp num_t = (i, j) -> i * N + j
    B[i, j]:  temp num_t = (i, j) -> i * N + j

parameters:

    TI_init:  int                 # tile size for i in SPD initialization
    TJ_init:  int                 # tile size for j in SPD initialization
    TT_init:  int                 # tile size for t (inner product) in SPD init

    # ================================================================
    # Stage 1: Build lower‑triangular A0 (Polybench init_array kernel)
    # ================================================================
    #
    # C reference:
    #   for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    #     for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
    #       A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
    #     for (j = i+1; j < n; j++)
    #       A[i][j] = 0;
    #     A[i][i] = 1;
    #   }
    #
    # For 0 <= j < n, (-j % n) == -j, so we can drop the modulus.
    init_lower:
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, N):
                if j < i:
                    A0[i, j] = (-cast<num_t>(j) / cast<num_t>(N)) + cast<num_t>(1)
                if j == i:
                    A0[i, j] = cast<num_t>(1)
                if j > i:
                    A0[i, j] = cast<num_t>(0)

    # ================================================================
    # Stage 2: Make matrix symmetric positive definite
    # ================================================================
    #
    # C reference:
    #   for (r = 0; r < n; r++)
    #     for (s = 0; s < n; s++) {
    #       B[r][s] = 0;
    #       for (t = 0; t < n; t++)
    #         B[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    #     }
    #   for (r,s) A[r][s] = B[r][s];
    #
    # Written in terms of A0 and B.
    spd_product:
        for i, j:
            B[i, j] = cast<num_t>(0)
            B[i, j] += sum(t in [0, N)):
                A0[i, t] * A0[j, t]

    copy_B_to_A:
        for i, j:
            A[i, j] = B[i, j]

    # ================================================================
    # Stage 3: In‑place LU factorization (no pivoting)
    # ================================================================
    #
    # C reference:
    #   for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    #     for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {
    #       for (k = 0; k < j; k++)
    #         A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
    #       A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
    #     }
    #     for (j = i; j < n; j++) {
    #       for (k = 0; k < i; k++)
    #         A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
    #     }
    #   }
    #
    # After completion:
    #   - Strict lower triangle of A holds L with unit diagonal.
    #   - Upper triangle (including diagonal) holds U.
    lu_factorization:
        # i (panel index) must be processed sequentially because later
        # panels depend on earlier ones.
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            # ---------------------------
            # L‑panel: j = 0 .. i‑1
            # ---------------------------
            lu_L_panel:
                for j in seq([0, i)):
                    # tmp_L = sum_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i,k] * A[k,j]
                    tmp_L = sum(k in [0, j)):
                        A[i, k] * A[k, j]
                    # A[i][j] = (A[i][j] - tmp_L) / A[j][j]
                    A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - tmp_L) / A[j, j]

            # ---------------------------
            # U‑row: j = i .. N‑1
            # ---------------------------
            lu_U_row:
                # For fixed i, all j in [i, N) are independent given that
                # lu_L_panel(i, *) is finished, so this loop can be parallel.
                for j in [i, N):
                    # tmp_U = sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i,k] * A[k,j]
                    tmp_U = sum(k in [0, i)):
                        A[i, k] * A[k, j]
                    # A[i][j] -= tmp_U
                    A[i, j] = A[i, j] - tmp_U

    # Initialization: A0 -> B -> A

        spd_product(i, j) -> copy_B_to_A(i, j)

    # Each U‑row element A[i,j] (j >= i) depends on all L‑panel entries
    # A[i,0..i‑1] in that row, but not on other U‑row entries A[i,j'].
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):

    # ================================================================
    # General notes
    # ================================================================
    # - Work is dominated by the SPD product and the O(N^3) LU updates.
    # - We improve temporal/spatial locality with blocking (tiling),
    #   reduce arithmetic latency with SIMD/vectorization over reductions,
    #   and exploit parallelism where true dependencies allow it.
    # - Extra storage is limited to A0 and B (O(N^2)), matching the
    #   Polybench reference’s A/B footprint (no >50% memory growth).
    # - Tile and vector widths (TI_*, TJ_*, TK_*, VEC_*) are tunable.

    # ================================================================
    # Stage 1: lower‑triangular initialization of A0
    # ================================================================
    # Simple loop with cheap arithmetic; we only add coarse tiling to
    # improve cache/TLB behavior for very large N.
    block(i, I_init, TI_init)        # tile rows of A0
    block(j, J_init, TJ_init)        # tile columns of A0
    hoist(I_init)                    # outermost over row tiles
    hoist(J_init)                    # then over column tiles
    # Inner scalar loops remain as‑is; no SIMD here (branches per element).

    # ================================================================
    # Stage 2: SPD product B = A0 * A0^T
    # ================================================================
    # Treat as blocked matrix multiplication over tiles of B.
    block(i, I_spd, TI_init)
    block(j, J_spd, TJ_init)
    block(t, T_spd, TT_init)

    # Process tiles in I_spd, J_spd, then accumulate over T_spd.
    hoist(I_spd)
    hoist(J_spd)
    hoist(T_spd)

    # Tiles (I_spd, J_spd) are independent; parallelize across them.
    parallelize(I_spd)
    parallelize(J_spd)

    # Vectorize the inner reduction over t within each tile to exploit
    # SIMD FMA on the contiguous A0[i, t] / A0[j, t] streams.
    vectorize(T_spd, VEC_T_init)

    # (Optional, if exact FP reproducibility is not required)
    #   Because B is symmetric, one could restrict to i <= j:
    #     if i <= j: compute B[i,j] as above; then set B[j,i] = B[i,j].
    #   This halves flops but slightly changes rounding behavior.
    #   We leave it commented‑out to preserve strict semantics.

    # ================================================================
    # Stage 3: copy B to A
    # ================================================================
    # Trivially parallel elementwise copy.
    parallelize(i)
    # Maintain contiguous inner loop on j for row‑major A/B.
    block(j, J_copy, TJ_init)
    hoist(J_copy)

    # ================================================================
    # Stage 4: LU factorization
    # ================================================================
    # Data‑dependence constraints:
    #   - i (panel index) must remain sequential.
    #   - j in lu_L_panel must remain sequential for each i.
    #   - j in lu_U_row can be parallelized for each fixed i.
    #   - Reductions over k can be tiled and vectorized.

    # ---- Panel blocking over i ----
    # Block rows into panels to improve reuse of the working set during
    # trailing updates. Within each panel, the scalar i loop remains seq.
    block(i, I_lu, TI_lu)
    hoist(I_lu)                      # outermost over panels

    # ---- L‑panel (j < i) optimizations ----
    block(k, K_L, TK_lu)             # tile k‑reduction
    hoist(K_L)                       # iterate over k‑tiles outer to scalar k
    vectorize(K_L, VEC_K_lu)         # SIMD over k within each tile
    # j in lu_L_panel is explicitly sequential (no parallelize(j)).

    # ---- U‑row (j >= i) optimizations ----
    block(j, J_U, TJ_lu)             # tile columns of U‑row
    hoist(J_U)

    # For fixed i, tiles J_U are independent; parallelize across them.
    parallelize(J_U)

    block(k, K_U, TK_lu)             # tile k‑reduction here as well
    hoist(K_U)
    vectorize(K_U, VEC_K_lu)         # SIMD over k within each tile

    # Within each J_U tile, small unroll of j to keep A[i, *] in registers.
    unroll(j, 2)                     # small factor (2 or 4 typical)

    # Note: we intentionally do *not* parallelize I_lu or i itself to
    # maintain the required row‑by‑row dependency order of LU.

    # We do *not* need to store this explicitly; it can be recomputed on the fly from (i, j, N).

        # Semantics:

        #   if j = i:  L[i, j] = 1

parameters:

    # Tunable block sizes / vector width (chosen based on CPU cache hierarchy & SIMD width)

    TJ_SPD: int                 # tile size for SPD init along j
    TT_SPD: int                 # tile size for SPD init along t
    VEC_SPD: int                # SIMD width for SPD inner loop over j (contiguous dimension)
    TK_LU: int                  # tile size for LU inner products over k
    UNROLL_L: int               # unroll factor for L-part k-loop
    UNROLL_U: int               # unroll factor for U-part k-loop

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Initialization: build symmetric positive-definite A = L * Lᵀ
    #    Matches init_array(): lower-triangular L followed by B = L * Lᵀ, then A := B.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1.1 Define conceptual lower-triangular L (not necessarily stored in memory)
    for i, j:
        L_init(i, j):
            if j > i:
                L[i, j] = 0
            else if j == i:
                L[i, j] = 1
            else:
                # For 0 <= j < N: (-j % N) / N + 1 == (-j / N) + 1
                L[i, j] = (-cast<DATA_TYPE>(j) / cast<DATA_TYPE>(N)) + cast<DATA_TYPE>(1)

    # 1.2 Build A as A = L * Lᵀ
    #     B[r][s] = Σ_t L[r][t] * L[s][t]; then copy B to A.
    #     Here we write directly into A.
    for i, j:
        SPD_build(i, j):
            A[i, j] = sum(t in [0, N)) (L[i, t] * L[j, t])

    # After SPD_build, A is symmetric positive-definite and no longer needs L.

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. LU factorization without pivoting (in-place, Doolittle-style)
    #
    # Original C:
    #   for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    #     for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {
    #       for (k = 0; k < j; k++)
    #         A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
    #       A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
    #     }
    #     for (j = i; j < n; j++) {
    #       for (k = 0; k < i; k++)
    #         A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
    #     }
    #   }
    #
    # We express this in two phases per row i:
    #   - L-part: j < i  (computing L[i,j] then dividing by A[j,j])
    #   - U-part: j >= i (updating row i of U)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    for i in seq(0, N):                    # i is strictly sequential
        # 2.1 L-part: compute A[i, j] for j < i
        for j in seq(0, i):                # j strictly sequential for j < i
            if j < i:
                LU_L(i, j):
                    # dot_L = Σ_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i,k] * A[k,j]
                    dot_L = sum(k_L in [0, j)) (A[i, k_L] * A[k_L, j])
                    # A[i,j] ← (A[i,j] - dot_L) / A[j,j]
                    A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_L) / A[j, j]

        # 2.2 U-part: compute A[i, j] for j >= i
        for j in seq(i, N):                # base algorithm is sequential; see optimization for parallelization
            LU_U(i, j):
                # dot_U = Σ_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i,k] * A[k,j]
                dot_U = sum(k_U in [0, i)) (A[i, k_U] * A[k_U, j])
                # A[i,j] ← A[i,j] - dot_U
                A[i, j] = A[i, j] - dot_U

    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i - 1):

    # 2.3 Inter-row dependencies: row i depends on all previous rows k < i.

        LU_U(i - 1, j_prev) -> LU_U(i, j)   # ensures completed row (i-1) is visible

    # =========================================================================
    # SPD stage optimizations: A = L * Lᵀ
    # =========================================================================
    # - This is a dense symmetric matrix-matrix multiply.
    # - Fully parallelizable across (i, j) because each A[i,j] is independent.
    # - We aggressively tile and parallelize this stage to exploit all cores.
    # - L is not stored in memory; we recompute its simple formula in registers.

    # 1. Tile i, j, and t to improve cache reuse and enable parallelization.
    block(i, I_SPD, TI_SPD)      # i = I_SPD * TI_SPD + i_inner
    block(j, J_SPD, TJ_SPD)      # j = J_SPD * TJ_SPD + j_inner
    block(t, T_SPD, TT_SPD)      # t = T_SPD * TT_SPD + t_inner

    # 2. Hoist the tile iterators outward to form a 3-level blocking:
    #      for I_SPD, J_SPD in outer loops (parallel)
    #          for T_SPD for shared L[i,t]/L[j,t] tiles
    #              inner micro-kernel on (i_inner, j_inner, t_inner)
    hoist(I_SPD)
    hoist(J_SPD)
    hoist(T_SPD)

    # 3. Parallelize across output tiles; each (I_SPD, J_SPD) pair is independent.
    parallelize(I_SPD)
    # Optionally also parallelize J_SPD for 2D tiling on NUMA / manycore:
    # parallelize(J_SPD)

    # 4. Vectorize across contiguous j dimension within a tile.
    #    Row-major A[i, j] means j is the fastest-varying index in memory.
    vectorize(j, VEC_SPD)

    # =========================================================================
    # LU factorization optimizations
    # =========================================================================
    # This stage is fundamentally sequential in i and in the L-part j < i loop.
    # We focus on:
    #   - improving inner dot-products with blocking, vectorization, unrolling
    #   - exploiting limited parallelism in the U-part across j ≥ i for fixed i

    # -------------------------------
    # 2.1 L-part (j < i)
    # -------------------------------
    # Inner reduction: dot_L = Σ_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i,k] * A[k,j]
    # A[i,k] is contiguous in k (row-major), so we tile and vectorize k.

    # Tile k for cache locality when j is large, and make a micro-kernel on TK_LU.
    block(k_L, K_L_TILE, TK_LU)        # k_L = K_L_TILE * TK_LU + k_L_inner

    # Unroll the small inner k_L_inner loop for better ILP within the dot-product.
    unroll(k_L_inner, UNROLL_L)

    # Vectorize along k_L_inner when TK_LU is a multiple of SIMD width.
    vectorize(k_L_inner, VEC_LU)

    # The (i, j) loop ordering stays sequential to respect dependencies.
    # No parallelization on i or j here.

    # -------------------------------
    # 2.2 U-part (j ≥ i)
    # -------------------------------
    # Inner reduction: dot_U = Σ_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i,k] * A[k,j]
    # For a fixed row i, all j ≥ i are independent once L row i is done,
    # because U-part never reads A[i,j'] for j' ≥ i. We exploit this.

    # Tile j and parallelize across column tiles for each fixed row i.
    block(j, J_LU, TJ_LU)              # j = J_LU * TJ_LU + j_inner
    parallelize(J_LU)                  # parallelism across column tiles per row i

    # Reuse the same k tiling and vectorization as in the L-part.
    block(k_U, K_U_TILE, TK_LU)
    unroll(k_U_inner, UNROLL_U)
    vectorize(k_U_inner, VEC_LU)

    # Note: The U-part still loops i sequentially, but within each i:
    #   - column tiles J_LU run in parallel
    #   - inner dot-products are vectorized and partially unrolled

    # =========================================================================
    # Memory and temporary storage considerations
    # =========================================================================
    # - L is conceptual only; we recompute its simple formula on the fly to avoid
    #   storing an extra N×N matrix. This keeps memory footprint ~1x A.
    # - Temporary accumulators (dot_L, dot_U) are scalar registers.
    # - Optionally, per-thread scratch buffers of size O(TK_LU) can be used to
    #   hold partial sums; this increases memory by at most O(#threads * TK_LU),
    #   which is negligible compared to N² and well below the +50% budget.

    N: dim in [0, N)

    #   A[i, j]  <->  C array A[i][j]

parameters:
    # Problem size (may also be compile-time)
    N: int

    # Precomputed scalar for initialization to avoid repeated divisions
    inv_N: num_t    # = 1 / (num_t) N

    # Tunable blocking & vectorization parameters for Phase 1 (SPD)
    TI_SPD: int     # tile size in r (e.g., 64)
    TJ_SPD: int     # tile size in s (e.g., 64)
    TT_SPD: int     # tile size in t (e.g., 64)
    VEC_SPD: int    # vector width along s (e.g., 8 or 16)

    # Tunable blocking & vectorization parameters for Phase 2 (LU)
    TJ_LU: int      # tile size in j_U for U-part (e.g., 64)
    VEC_LU_J: int   # vector width along j_U in U-part
    VEC_LU_K: int   # vector width / unroll factor along k_L, k_U (small, e.g., 4)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: implicit lower-triangular generator L(i, t)
    #
    # Original initialization:
    #   for i in 0..N-1:
    #     for j in 0..i:      A[i][j] = (-j % N)/N + 1
    #     for j in i+1..N-1:  A[i][j] = 0
    #     A[i][i] = 1
    #
    # For 0 <= j < N, (-j % N) == -j, so:
    #   L(i, j) = { 1                  if j == i
    #             { 1 - j/N            if j < i
    #             { 0                  if j > i
    #
    # We do not store L; we use this expression directly in the SPD step.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    # ==============================
    # Phase 1: SPD initialization
    # ==============================
    #
    # Make A symmetric positive definite:
    #   B[r][s] = sum_t L(r, t) * L(s, t)
    #   A[r][s] = B[r][s]
    #
    # We exploit symmetry and only compute r ≥ s, then mirror.
    #
    for r in [0, N):
        for s in [0, r + 1):                # s ≤ r; strictly lower + diagonal
            # Compute single entry via symmetric rank-1 updates:
            A[r, s] = sum(t in [0, N):
                             (   # L(r, t)
                                 (if t == r then 1
                                  else if t < r then (1 - t * inv_N)
                                  else 0)
                               *
                                 # L(s, t)
                                 (if t == s then 1
                                  else if t < s then (1 - t * inv_N)
                                  else 0)
                             )

            # Fill the symmetric counterpart A[s, r]:
            if s < r:
                A[s, r] = A[r, s]

    # At this point A holds the same SPD matrix as in the original init_array()
    # (up to floating-point evaluation order), but computed directly from the
    # analytic L(i, t) without ever storing L explicitly.

    # ============================
    # Phase 2: LU factorization
    # ============================
    #
    # Original C kernel (on A[i][j]):
    #
    # for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    #   for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {
    #     for (k = 0; k < j; k++)
    #       A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
    #     A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
    #   }
    #   for (j = i; j < n; j++) {
    #     for (k = 0; k < i; k++)
    #       A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
    #   }
    # }
    #
    # We express this directly, with explicit sum() for the reductions.
    # Note the dependence pattern:
    #   - outer loop i is strictly sequential
    #   - first j-loop (j < i) is sequential along j_L (each A[i,j_L] depends
    #     on all A[i,k_L] for k_L < j_L)
    #   - second j-loop (j >= i) has independent j_U iterations for fixed i.
    #

    # L-part (strictly lower triangular, j_L < i)
    for i in seq([0, N)):
        for j_L in seq([0, i)):
            # A[i, j_L] -= sum_{k_L < j_L} A[i, k_L] * A[k_L, j_L]
            A[i, j_L] = (A[i, j_L]
                         - sum(k_L in [0, j_L):
                                   A[i, k_L] * A[k_L, j_L])
                         ) / A[j_L, j_L]

        # U-part (upper including diagonal, j_U >= i)
        for j_U in [i, N):  # no loop-carried deps across j_U for fixed i
            # A[i, j_U] -= sum_{k_U < i} A[i, k_U] * A[k_U, j_U]
            A[i, j_U] = A[i, j_U]
                        - sum(k_U in [0, i):
                                   A[i, k_U] * A[k_U, j_U])

    # =========================================
    # Phase 1 (SPD initialization) optimizations
    # =========================================
    #
    # A[r, s] = sum_t L(r, t) * L(s, t)
    # is an all-pairs dot product, i.e., a symmetric matrix-multiply
    # A = L * L^T. We apply standard GEMM blocking and vectorization.

    # Block outer SPD loops for cache locality.
    # - I, J, T are the tile indices in r, s, t respectively.
    # - TI_SPD, TJ_SPD, TT_SPD are tunable tile sizes (e.g., 64).
    block(r, I_SPD, TI_SPD)
    block(s, J_SPD, TJ_SPD)
    block(t, T_SPD, TT_SPD)

    # Evaluate tiles in an order that maximizes reuse of L(·, t) values
    # across r and s; hoist tile indices outward.
    hoist(I_SPD)
    hoist(J_SPD)
    hoist(T_SPD)

    # Parallelize across row-tiles; SPD has no dependencies across rows.
    parallelize(I_SPD)

    # Vectorize along the innermost contiguous dimension s within each tile.
    # This maps directly to SIMD loads/stores for A[r, s] and L(s, t).
    vectorize(s, VEC_SPD)

    # Optionally unroll the reduction tile dimension for instruction-level
    # parallelism within a vectorized inner loop.
    unroll(T_SPD, 2)

    # ======================================
    # Phase 2 (LU factorization) optimizations
    # ======================================

    # --- Outer i-loop ---
    # i must be strictly sequential due to strong data dependencies between rows.
    # We preserve seq() on i and do not parallelize it.

    # --- L-part (j_L < i) ---
    # j_L also has loop-carried dependencies (A[i, j_L] uses A[i, k_L] for k_L < j_L),
    # so we keep j_L sequential. We only optimize the reduction over k_L.

    # Small unrolling/vectorization of the inner reduction improves throughput
    # for the dot product A[i, :] · column j_L.
    unroll(k_L, VEC_LU_K)
    # If the hardware supports it and the compiler can resolve dependencies,
    # vectorize the innermost reduction; this is safe because the sum is purely
    # associative and there are no cross-iteration dependencies in k_L.
    vectorize(k_L, VEC_LU_K)

    # --- U-part (j_U >= i) ---
    # For fixed i, the iterations over j_U are independent (each A[i, j_U]
    # only reads A[i, k_U] and A[k_U, j_U] for k_U < i, all already computed).
    # We can exploit both parallelism and SIMD across j_U.

    # Tile the j_U dimension for cache locality: process TJ_LU columns at a time.
    block(j_U, J_U_tile, TJ_LU)

    # Parallelize across column tiles for each i; this is safe as tiles are
    # independent writes to A[i, j_U].
    parallelize(J_U_tile)

    # Vectorize within each tile along j_U (contiguous dimension).
    vectorize(j_U, VEC_LU_J)

    # Unroll the reduction over k_U to improve ILP for each (i, j_U) pair.
    unroll(k_U, VEC_LU_K)

    # --------------------------------------
    # General arithmetic optimizations
    # --------------------------------------
    #
    # - Reuse inv_N in the SPD phase instead of recomputing 1/(num_t)N.
    #   This replaces repeated divisions by a single multiplication per use.
    #
    # - The analytic L(i, t) definition avoids ever materializing the initial
    #   lower-triangular matrix, reducing memory traffic relative to a

    #   initialization, computing A[r, s] only for s ≤ r and mirroring
    #   to A[s, r]. This preserves the exact mathematical result while

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    # Define the conceptual lower-triangular generator A_lower.
    # Matches the C/Polybench initialization (translated to 0-based indices):
    #   for i in 0..N-1:
    #     for j in 0..i:     A[i][j] = (-j % N) / N + 1   ; A[i][i] = 1
    #     for j in i+1..N-1: A[i][j] = 0
    #
    # Since 0 <= j < N, (-j % N) == -j, so we can drop % N.
    define_A_lower:
        for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
            A_lower[i, j] =
                if (j < i)  then (-cast<num_t>(j) / cast<num_t>(N) + cast<num_t>(1))
                else if (j == i) then cast<num_t>(1)
                else                cast<num_t>(0)

    # Now form a Gram matrix from these rows:
    #   A = A_lower * A_lower^T
    # i.e. A[i,j] = sum_t A_lower[i,t] * A_lower[j,t].
    init_spd:
        for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
            A[i, j] =
                sum(t in [0, N),
                    A_lower[i, t] * A_lower[j, t])

    #
    # Original C kernel:
    #   for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    #     for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {
    #       for (k = 0; k < j; k++)

    #       A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
    #     }
    #     for (j = i; j < n; j++) {
    #       for (k = 0; k < i; k++)
    #         A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
    #     }
    #   }
    #
    # We mirror this algorithm exactly, but expose reductions explicitly.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

            # ---- Lower-triangular part (L): 0 <= j < i

                    # A[i][j] -= sum_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i][k] * A[k][j]

                for j in [0, i]:

            # ---- Upper-triangular part (U): i <= j < N

                    tmp_U =
                        A[i, j] -
                        sum(k2 in [0, i),
                            row_i[k2] * A[k2, j])

                    A[i, j] = tmp_U

computation:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Initialization: construct a symmetric positive-definite matrix in A.
  #
  #    Matches init_array():
  #      - First define an implicit unit lower-triangular matrix A0:
  #          A0[i][t] =
  #             1                      if t == i
  #             1 - t / N              if t <  i
  #             0                      if t >  i
  #      - Then set A = A0 * A0^T:
  #          A[i][j] = sum_t A0[i][t] * A0[j][t]
  #
  #    We never materialize A0 as a separate array; it is an inline expression.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  for i, j:
    A[i, j] =
      sum(t in [0, N)):
        (  (t == i) * DATA_TYPE(1)
         + (t <  i) * (DATA_TYPE(1) - DATA_TYPE(t) / DATA_TYPE(N))
         + (t >  i) * DATA_TYPE(0) ) *
        (  (t == j) * DATA_TYPE(1)
         + (t <  j) * (DATA_TYPE(1) - DATA_TYPE(t) / DATA_TYPE(N))
         + (t >  j) * DATA_TYPE(0) )

  # After this phase A is exactly B = A0 * A0^T as in the Halide init_array().

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. In‑place LU factorization of A.
  #
  #    Algorithm (Doolittle with unit-diagonal L), identical to the C kernel:
  #
  #    for i = 0..N-1:
  #      // L-part: j < i
  #      for j = 0..i-1:
  #        A[i][j] = (A[i][j] - sum_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i][k] * A[k][j]) / A[j][j]
  #
  #      // U-part: j >= i
  #      for j = i..N-1:
  #        A[i][j] = A[i][j] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i][k] * A[k][j]
  #
  #    All loop-carried dependences on i and on j in the L-part are preserved.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # 2a. L part (j < i): strictly sequential in i and in j.
  for i in seq[0, N):
    for j in seq[0, i):
      A[i, j] =
        (A[i, j] -
           sum(k in [0, j)):
             A[i, k] * A[k, j]) / A[j, j]

  # 2b. U part (j >= i): for each fixed i, all j in [i, N) are independent.
  for i in seq[0, N):
    for j in [i, N):
      A[i, j] =
        A[i, j] -
          sum(k in [0, i)):
            A[i, k] * A[k, j]

  # Initialization (SPD construction A = A0 * A0^T)

  # Treat this as a symmetric matrix–matrix multiplication and optimize it
  # similarly to GEMM, while preserving arithmetic order of the inner sum.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # Tile i, j, t to improve cache reuse of implicit A0 rows/columns.

  block(j, J_init, TJ_init)    # outer tiles over columns of A
  block(t, T_init, TT_init)    # inner tiles over reduction dimension t

  # Make the tile loops outermost and keep the inner t-loop contiguous.
  hoist(I_init)
  hoist(J_init)

  # Vectorize over t inside the innermost accumulation loop to exploit SIMD.
  vectorize(T_init, VEC_T_init)

  # Light unrolling in t for additional ILP.
  unroll(T_init, factor = 2)

  # Parallelize tiles in the i-dimension across CPU cores.
  # J_init stays sequential per task to avoid nested parallelism.
  parallelize(I_init)

  # NOTE: A is mathematically symmetric after this phase, but we deliberately
  # do not exploit symmetry (e.g., computing only j >= i) to keep the
  # reduction order identical to the original code. An implementation that
  # tolerates small FP differences could additionally cut work by ≈2×.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # LU factorization
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # L part (j < i):
  #   - i and j must remain sequential due to triangluar dependencies.
  #   - Only k (the reduction) can be optimized.
  unroll(k, UK_L)        # unroll inner dot-product in L-part
  vectorize(k, VEC_K)    # SIMD over k where hardware supports it

  # U part (j >= i):
  #   For each fixed i, the updates of A[i, j] are independent across j.
  #   We can tile and parallelize j, and also optimize the k reduction.

  block(j, J_U, BJ_U)    # tile columns for better cache locality
  parallelize(J_U)       # run column tiles of the U-part in parallel

  # Re-express the U-part reduction as a rank-1 (outer-product) style update
  # by interchanging the k and j loops within the sum:
  #
  #   Original (per j):
  #     A[i,j] -= sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i,k] * A[k,j]
  #
  #   Optimized (per k):
  #     for k in [0, i):
  #       for j in [i, N):
  #         A[i,j] -= A[i,k] * A[k,j]
  #
  #   This is mathematically equivalent to the sum over k, improves reuse
  #   of A[i,k] and row k of U, and aligns memory access along j.
  interchange(k, j)      # apply only to the U-part’s inner loops

  # Within the U-part, also exploit ILP and SIMD on k.
  unroll(k, UK_U)
  vectorize(k, VEC_K)

  hoist(i)               # ensure no reordering moves work outside the i-loop
